---
title: "Project 2: Melbourne Housing Data Exploration"
format: html
editor: visual
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

#Import and inspect
housing_raw <- read_csv("data/Melbourne_housing_FULL.csv", show_col_types = FALSE )
glimpse(housing_raw)
summary(housing_raw)
```

The Melbourne housing dataset contains 34,857 records and 21 variables describing property characteristics, locations, sale methods, and prices. Among records with observed prices, the median price is A\$870,000 and the mean is approximately A\$1.05 million. The higher mean and maximum price of A\$11.2 million suggest a right-skewed distribution. Prices are missing for 7,610 records (21.8%), so price analyses will use only records with observed prices. Building area and year built also have substantial missingness, and some values warrant further investigation, including construction years ranging from 1196 to 2106 and unusually large land and building areas. The analysis will explore how prices vary across property types and regions and how they relate to distance from the city centre, building area, and room count.

Questions to explore:

1\. How do prices differ across property types and regions?

2\. How does the mix of property types vary across regions?

3\. How is price associated with distance from the city center?

4\. How are building area and room count associated with price?

# 

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Confirm the variables needed below are available.

required_columns \<- c( "Type", "Regionname", "Price", "Rooms", "Distance", "Bathroom", "BuildingArea" )

stopifnot(all(required_columns %in% names(housing_raw)))

# Missing-data summary

missing_summary \<- housing_raw \|\> summarise(across(everything(), \~ sum(is.na(.x)))) \|\> pivot_longer( everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "missing_n" ) \|\> mutate(missing_pct = 100 \* missing_n / nrow(housing_raw)) \|\> arrange(desc(missing_pct))

print(missing_summary, n = Inf)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2. Prepare variables

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

housing \<- housing_raw \|\> mutate( property_type = factor( Type, levels = c("h", "t", "u"), labels = c("House", "Townhouse", "Unit/apartment") ), region = na_if(str_trim(Regionname), ""), region = factor(region), \# Treat nonpositive values as unavailable for these measures. Price = if_else(Price \> 0, Price, NA_real\_), BuildingArea = if_else(BuildingArea \> 0, BuildingArea, NA_real\_) )

# Retain records without prices for counts of recorded properties.

# Use records with observed prices for price analyses.

priced \<- housing \|\> filter(!is.na(Price))

sample_sizes \<- tibble( measure = c( "All records", "Records with observed positive prices", "Records without usable prices" ), n = c( nrow(housing), nrow(priced), sum(is.na(housing\$Price)) ) )

print(sample_sizes)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# 3. One-way contingency tables

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

type_counts \<- housing \|\> count(property_type, name = "n", .drop = FALSE) \|\> mutate(percent = 100 \* n / sum(n))

region_counts \<- housing \|\> count(region, name = "n", sort = TRUE) \|\> mutate(percent = 100 \* n / sum(n))

print(type_counts) print(region_counts)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# 4. Two-way contingency tables

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Property type by region

type_region_table \<- with( housing, table(region, property_type, useNA = "ifany") )

print(addmargins(type_region_table))

# Within-region percentages, using records with known categories

type_region_complete \<- housing \|\> filter(!is.na(region), !is.na(property_type))

type_region_pct \<- with( type_region_complete, prop.table(table(region, property_type), margin = 1) \* 100 )

print(round(type_region_pct, 1))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# 5. Numerical summaries

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Overall price summary

overall_price_summary \<- priced \|\> summarise( n = n(), mean_price = mean(Price), median_price = median(Price), sd_price = sd(Price), q1_price = quantile(Price, 0.25), q3_price = quantile(Price, 0.75), min_price = min(Price), max_price = max(Price) )

print(overall_price_summary)

# Price summaries by property type

price_by_type \<- priced \|\> filter(!is.na(property_type)) \|\> group_by(property_type) \|\> summarise( n = n(), mean_price = mean(Price), median_price = median(Price), sd_price = sd(Price), IQR_price = IQR(Price), .groups = "drop" )

print(price_by_type)

# Price summaries by region AND property type

price_by_region_type \<- priced \|\> filter(!is.na(region), !is.na(property_type)) \|\> group_by(region, property_type) \|\> summarise( n = n(), mean_price = mean(Price), median_price = median(Price), sd_price = sd(Price), .groups = "drop" )

print(price_by_region_type, n = Inf)

# Multiple quantitative variables at levels of property type

quantitative_by_type \<- housing \|\> filter(!is.na(property_type)) \|\> select( property_type, Price, Rooms, Distance, Bathroom, BuildingArea ) \|\> pivot_longer( -property_type, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value" ) \|\> group_by(property_type, variable) \|\> summarise( n_observed = sum(!is.na(value)), mean = if (all(is.na(value))) NA_real\_ else mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), median = if (all(is.na(value))) NA_real\_ else median(value, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop" )

print(quantitative_by_type, n = Inf)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# 6. Plot settings

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

type_colors \<- c( "House" = "#0072B2", "Townhouse" = "#D55E00", "Unit/apartment" = "#009E73" )

price_labels \<- label_dollar( prefix = "A\$", scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M" )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Plot 1: Bar chart

# Univariate: property type

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

p1 \<- housing \|\> filter(!is.na(property_type)) \|\> ggplot(aes(x = property_type)) + geom_bar(fill = "#0072B2", width = 0.65) + labs( title = "Houses, Townhouses, and Units in the Dataset", x = "Property type", y = "Number of records" )

print(p1)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Plot 2: Side-by-side bar chart

# Multivariate: region and property type

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

p2 \<- type_region_complete \|\> ggplot(aes(x = region, fill = property_type)) + geom_bar(position = "dodge") + coord_flip() + scale_fill_manual(values = type_colors) + labs( title = "Property Types Across Melbourne Regions", x = "Region", y = "Number of records", fill = "Property type" )

print(p2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Plot 3: Histogram

# Univariate: price

# A log scale helps show a right-skewed price distribution.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

p3 \<- ggplot(priced, aes(x = Price)) + geom_histogram( bins = 40, fill = "#0072B2", color = "white" ) + scale_x_log10(labels = price_labels) + labs( title = "Distribution of Observed Melbourne Property Prices", subtitle = "Price axis uses a logarithmic scale", x = "Price (AUD; log scale)", y = "Number of records" )

print(p3)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Plot 4: Box plot

# Multivariate: property type and price

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

p4 \<- priced \|\> filter(!is.na(property_type)) \|\> ggplot(aes( x = property_type, y = Price, fill = property_type )) + geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.15) + scale_fill_manual(values = type_colors) + scale_y_log10(labels = price_labels) + labs( title = "Property Prices by Property Type", subtitle = "Price axis uses a logarithmic scale", x = "Property type", y = "Price (AUD; log scale)" ) + theme(legend.position = "none")

print(p4)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Plot 5: Scatter plot

# Multivariate: distance, price, and property type

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

p5 \<- priced \|\> filter(!is.na(Distance), !is.na(property_type)) \|\> ggplot(aes( x = Distance, y = Price, color = property_type )) + geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 1) + scale_color_manual(values = type_colors) + scale_y_log10(labels = price_labels) + labs( title = "Property Prices and Distance from Central Melbourne", subtitle = "Each point represents one record with an observed price", x = "Distance from city centre (km)", y = "Price (AUD; log scale)", color = "Property type" )

print(p5)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Plot 6: Faceted scatter plot

# Multivariate: building area, price, type, and room count

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

p6 \<- priced \|\> filter( !is.na(BuildingArea), !is.na(property_type), !is.na(Rooms) ) \|\> ggplot(aes( x = BuildingArea, y = Price, color = Rooms )) + geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 1) + facet_wrap(\~ property_type) + scale_color_viridis_c(option = "C") + scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma()) + scale_y_log10(labels = price_labels) + labs( title = "Building Area and Price Across Property Types", subtitle = "Both axes use logarithmic scales; color shows room count", x = "Building area (square metres; log scale)", y = "Price (AUD; log scale)", color = "Rooms" )

print(p6)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Plot 7: Heatmap — additional plot type

# Multivariate: region, property type, and median price

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

heatmap_data \<- price_by_region_type \|\> mutate( price_label = paste0( dollar(median_price, scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M"), "\nn = ", comma(n) ) )

p7 \<- ggplot( heatmap_data, aes( x = property_type, y = region, fill = median_price ) ) + geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) + geom_text(aes(label = price_label), size = 3) + scale_fill_gradient( low = "#F7FBFF", high = "#6BAED6", labels = price_labels ) + labs( title = "Median Property Price by Region and Property Type", subtitle = "Each tile shows the median price and number of observed prices", x = "Property type", y = "Region", fill = "Median price\n(AUD)" ) + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

print(p7)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# 7. Save summaries and figures

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

dir.create("output", showWarnings = FALSE) dir.create("output/figures", showWarnings = FALSE)

write_csv(missing_summary, "output/missing_summary.csv") write_csv(sample_sizes, "output/sample_sizes.csv") write_csv(type_counts, "output/property_type_counts.csv") write_csv(region_counts, "output/region_counts.csv") write_csv(overall_price_summary, "output/overall_price_summary.csv") write_csv(price_by_type, "output/price_by_type.csv") write_csv(price_by_region_type, "output/price_by_region_type.csv") write_csv(quantitative_by_type, "output/quantitative_by_type.csv")

write.csv( as.data.frame.matrix(type_region_table), "output/type_by_region_counts.csv" )

write.csv( round(type_region_pct, 1), "output/type_by_region_percentages.csv" )

plots \<- list( property_type_bar = p1, region_type_bars = p2, price_histogram = p3, price_type_boxplot = p4, price_distance_scatter = p5, price_area_faceted = p6, median_price_heatmap = p7 )

iwalk( plots, \~ ggsave( filename = file.path( "output/figures", paste0(.y, ".png") ), plot = .x, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300 ) )
